spelling.title: Spelling

detail.aboutTemplate: Let’s learn to spell {name} — listen to each letter!
detail.funFactTemplate: Every letter in {name} has its own sound!
detail.tryTemplate: Spell {name} slowly in the air, one letter at a time!

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is an animal — it can move, eat, and many make fun sounds!
detail.funFactTemplate: Some animals are pets, some live on farms, and some in the wild!
detail.tryTemplate: Spell {name} in the air! Can you copy the animal’s sound?

dog.about: {name} is a friendly pet that many families keep at home. It has soft fur, a wagging tail, and four legs for running. {name} loves to play with you and barks when excited.
dog.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can smell much better than you can! Its nose finds food and people far away. Some dogs help police and farmers.

cat.about: {name} is a quiet pet with soft fur and whiskers on its face. It likes sunny spots for naps and purrs when happy. {name} can climb and loves to chase toys.
cat.funFact: Did you know? A {name} uses its whiskers to feel things in the dark! Cats can jump high and land softly on their paws. A cat's tongue feels rough like a brush.

lion.about: {name} is a big wild cat with a golden mane on the males. It lives on grassy plains in Africa and roars very loudly. {name} hunts with its family group called a pride.
lion.funFact: Did you know? A {name}'s roar can be heard from far away! Lions rest most of the day and hunt more at night. Every lion in a pride helps care for the cubs.
lion.try: Spell {name} and roar like a brave lion!

elephant.about: {name} is the biggest animal that walks on land. It has a long trunk to drink, splash water, and pick up food. {name} lives in herds and has big floppy ears.
elephant.funFact: Did you know? An {name} never forgets friends and places! Its trunk has thousands of muscles. Elephants use their feet to feel vibrations far away.
elephant.try: Spell {name} and swing your arm like a trunk!

panda.about: {name} is a black-and-white bear that lives in mountain forests in China. It has round black eye patches and loves to eat bamboo. {name} spends most of the day chewing stems and leaves.
panda.funFact: Did you know? A baby {name} is tiny and pink when born! Giant pandas eat bamboo almost all day long. They are very good at climbing trees.
panda.try: Spell {name} and munch your hands like eating bamboo!

monkey.about: {name} is a playful animal that lives in trees in warm forests. It has long arms and a long tail for balance. {name} swings on branches and uses its hands to grab fruit.
monkey.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s use sticks to find insects! Monkeys live in groups and groom each other's fur. They make many sounds to talk to friends.
monkey.try: Spell {name} and scratch your head like a monkey!

rabbit.about: {name} is a small furry animal with long ears and a fluffy tail. It hops on strong back legs and likes to eat carrots and grass. {name} lives in burrows under the ground.
rabbit.funFact: Did you know? A {name}'s teeth keep growing its whole life! Rabbits can hear sounds from very far away. They thump their back feet to warn friends of danger.

fox.about: {name} is a clever wild animal with a bushy tail and pointy ears. Its fur is often reddish-orange with a white tip on the tail. {name} hunts at night and lives in forests and fields.
fox.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can hear a tiny mouse under the snow! Foxes have excellent night vision. They store extra food to eat later.
fox.try: Spell {name} and tiptoe quietly like a sly fox!

bear.about: {name} is a big, strong animal with thick fur for cold places. It has sharp claws and a short tail. {name} eats fish, berries, and honey and can climb trees.
bear.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s sleep all winter in a cozy den! A bear's sense of smell is very strong. Bear cubs stay close to their mother.
bear.try: Spell {name} and give yourself a big bear hug!

tiger.about: {name} has bright orange fur with black stripes all over its body. It is a powerful hunter that lives in jungles and grasslands. {name} swims well and likes to hide in tall grass.
tiger.funFact: Did you know? Every {name}'s stripe pattern is unique, like your fingerprint! Tigers can jump very far to catch prey. They are the biggest cats in the wild.
tiger.try: Spell {name} and walk softly like a tiger!

zebra.about: {name} looks like a horse covered in black-and-white stripes. It lives in herds on African grasslands and eats grass all day. {name} runs fast to escape lions.
zebra.funFact: Did you know? No two {name}s have exactly the same stripes! Zebras sleep standing up sometimes. Their stripes may confuse biting flies.
zebra.try: Spell {name} and draw stripes in the air with your finger!

giraffe.about: {name} is the tallest animal in the world with a very long neck. It eats leaves from the tops of acacia trees on the savanna. {name} has long legs and small horns on its head.
giraffe.funFact: Did you know? A {name}'s tongue is dark purple and very long! It can clean its ears with its tongue. Giraffes only need a little sleep each day.
giraffe.try: Spell {name} and stretch your neck up high!

pig.about: {name} is a farm animal with a round snout and a curly tail. It likes to roll in mud to stay cool on hot days. {name} eats plants and scraps and snorts happily.
pig.funFact: Did you know? A {name} is very smart and can learn tricks! Pigs have an excellent sense of smell. Baby pigs are called piglets.

cow.about: {name} is a gentle farm animal that gives us milk. It has four stomach parts to digest grass and chews slowly. {name} lives in fields and says "moo" to its herd.
cow.funFact: Did you know? A {name} chews its food twice — that is called chewing the cud! Cows can see almost all the way around without turning their head. They like to stay in a herd.
cow.try: Spell {name} and say "moo" after each letter!

horse.about: {name} is a strong animal people ride and use on farms. It has a long mane, hooves, and can gallop very fast. {name} eats hay and grass and likes open fields.
horse.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can sleep standing up! Horses communicate with their ears and tails. They can run soon after they are born.

sheep.about: {name} is a fluffy farm animal covered in soft wool. Farmers shear its wool to make warm clothes. {name} eats grass and stays close to its flock.
sheep.funFact: Did you know? A {name} remembers faces for years! Sheep have rectangular pupils in their eyes. Lambs can walk soon after birth.

goat.about: {name} is a clever farm animal with horns and a beard sometimes. It climbs rocky hills and loves to nibble leaves and grass. {name} can balance on steep places.
goat.funFact: Did you know? A {name} has rectangular pupils like a sheep! Goats are curious and like to explore. They can yell loudly to call their friends.
goat.try: Spell {name} and pretend to climb a little hill!

deer.about: {name} is a gentle wild animal with slim legs and a light body. Male deer often grow antlers on their head that look like branches. {name} lives in forests and can jump very high.
deer.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can jump higher than a tall grown-up! Its big ears hear tiny sounds far away. Deer run quickly to escape danger.
deer.try: Spell {name} and leap gently like a deer!

camel.about: {name} is a tall animal made for hot, sandy deserts. It has one or two humps that store fat for long trips. {name} has long eyelashes and wide feet that do not sink in sand.
camel.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can drink lots of water at once and save it inside! Camels can close their nostrils in sandstorms. People have used camels to carry loads for thousands of years.
camel.try: Spell {name} and walk slowly like crossing hot sand!

wolf.about: {name} is a wild dog-like animal that lives in a family pack. Pack members howl to talk, especially at night. {name} has sharp teeth, strong legs, and thick fur for cold forests.
wolf.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can run a very long time without getting tired! The pack hunts together using teamwork. Wolves usually stay far from towns.

gorilla.about: {name} is a huge ape with long arms and dark fur. It lives in African rainforests and eats leaves and fruit. {name} beats its chest and walks on its knuckles.
gorilla.funFact: Did you know? A {name} is mostly gentle and shy around people! Gorillas build nests to sleep in each night. They are very smart and use tools.
gorilla.try: Spell {name} and thump your chest softly!

kangaroo.about: {name} is an Australian animal that hops on strong back legs. The mother carries her tiny baby in a pouch on her belly. {name} eats grass and lives in open country.
kangaroo.funFact: Did you know? A {name} cannot walk backwards easily! Kangaroos can jump very far in one leap. A baby kangaroo is called a joey.
kangaroo.try: Spell {name} and hop with both feet together!

hippo.about: {name} is a huge gray animal that spends lots of time in rivers. It looks heavy but swims and holds its breath underwater. {name} has big teeth and eats grass at night.
hippo.funFact: Did you know? A {name}'s mouth can open wider than you might think! Hippos sweat a pinkish liquid that works like sunscreen. They are one of the heaviest land animals.
hippo.try: Spell {name} and yawn with a big open mouth!

rhino.about: {name} is a big gray animal with thick skin like armor. It has one or two horns on its nose made of keratin. {name} eats grass and lives on grasslands in Africa and Asia.
rhino.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can run surprisingly fast! Rhinos have poor eyesight but a great sense of smell. Their horns keep growing.
rhino.try: Spell {name} and march slowly like a strong rhino!

leopard.about: {name} is a spotted wild cat that climbs trees very well. It has golden fur with black rosette spots. {name} hunts at night and hides prey in branches.
leopard.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can drag prey heavier than itself up a tree! Leopards are great swimmers. Each spot pattern is unique.
leopard.try: Spell {name} and crouch low like a sneaky leopard!

squirrel.about: {name} is a small tree animal with a big fluffy tail. It climbs quickly and hides nuts for winter. {name} has sharp front teeth and busy little paws.
squirrel.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can jump between branches very far! Some squirrels pretend to bury nuts to trick thieves. Their tail helps them balance.
squirrel.try: Spell {name} and twitch your nose like a busy squirrel!

hedgehog.about: {name} is a small animal with spiky spines on its back. When scared, it curls into a tight ball. {name} sniffs for insects at night in gardens and woods.
hedgehog.funFact: Did you know? A {name} has about 5,000 spines! It is immune to some snake venom. Hedgehogs can swim a little.
hedgehog.try: Spell {name} and curl up small like a spiky ball!

mouse.about: {name} is a tiny animal with a long tail and whiskers. It scurries quickly and likes to nibble seeds and crumbs. {name} often lives near people in quiet corners.
mouse.funFact: Did you know? A {name}'s teeth never stop growing! Mice can squeeze through very small holes. They use whiskers to feel their way in the dark.

hamster.about: {name} is a small furry pet with chubby cheeks. It stuffs food into its cheek pouches to carry home. {name} loves running on a wheel at night.
hamster.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can store food equal to half its body in its cheeks! Hamsters dig burrows in the wild. They like to hoard seeds.
hamster.try: Spell {name} and puff your cheeks full of air!

bat.about: {name} is the only mammal that can truly fly. It is awake at night and rests upside down in caves or trees. {name} eats insects and uses sound echoes to find them.
bat.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s eat fruit or nectar from flowers! Bat wings are made of skin stretched over finger bones. Bats help pollinate plants.
bat.try: Spell {name} and flap your arms like wings!

snake.about: {name} is a long animal with no legs that slithers on its belly. It flicks its tongue to smell the air. {name} lives in grass, deserts, forests, or water.
snake.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s shed their whole skin as they grow! Snakes swallow prey whole. They feel vibrations through the ground.
snake.try: Spell {name} and slither your arm side to side!

lizard.about: {name} is a reptile with scaly skin and a long tail. Many kinds love to sunbathe on warm rocks. {name} sticks out its tongue quickly to catch insects.
lizard.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s can regrow a lost tail! Lizards have eyelids unlike snakes. The chameleon can change color to hide.
lizard.try: Spell {name} and stick out your tongue quickly like a lizard!

frog.about: {name} is a hopping animal that lives near ponds and wet places. It starts life as a tadpole swimming in water. {name} has smooth wet skin and big eyes.
frog.funFact: Did you know? A {name} drinks water through its skin! Frogs catch flies with a sticky long tongue. Some frogs can jump many times their body length.

ant.about: {name} is a tiny insect but very strong for its size. It lives in a big underground home called a colony. {name} works with thousands of sisters to find food.
ant.funFact: Did you know? An {name} can carry many times its own weight! Ants leave scent trails so friends follow the path. Some ants farm aphids for sweet drops.
ant.try: Spell {name} and march in a tiny line with your fingers!

bee.about: {name} is a buzzing insect with yellow and black stripes. It flies from flower to flower and helps plants make fruit. {name} makes honey in a hive with its family.
bee.funFact: Did you know? A {name} dances to tell hive mates where flowers are! Bees see colors we cannot see. One bee visits hundreds of flowers a day.
bee.try: Spell {name} and buzz "zzzz" while you spell!

ladybug.about: {name} is a small round beetle that is often red with black spots. It eats tiny pests in gardens and is helpful to plants. {name} has hard shiny wings that fold over its back.
ladybug.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can pretend to be dead to trick predators! Ladybugs bleed a smelly yellow liquid from their legs when scared. They hibernate in big groups.
ladybug.try: Spell {name} and count the spots you imagine on its back!

butterfly.about: {name} starts as a caterpillar, then makes a chrysalis and grows wings. It has colorful wings and sips nectar with a long tongue. {name} flutters from flower to flower in sunshine.
butterfly.funFact: Did you know? A {name} tastes with its feet! Some butterflies migrate thousands of miles. Their wings are covered in tiny scales.
butterfly.try: Spell {name} and flutter your hands like wings!

spider.about: {name} has eight legs and spins silk webs to catch insects. It is not an insect — it has two body parts. {name} waits quietly or hunts on the ground.
spider.funFact: Did you know? {name} silk is very strong for how thin it is! Spiders replace their webs often. Jumping spiders can leap far to pounce.
spider.try: Spell {name} and wiggle eight fingers in the air!

scorpion.about: {name} has pincers like claws and a curved tail with a stinger. It glows green under a special black light. {name} hunts at night in deserts and hides under rocks.
scorpion.funFact: Did you know? {name}s have been on Earth since before dinosaurs! A mother scorpion carries babies on her back. They can slow their breathing to survive.
scorpion.try: Spell {name} and make pincers with your hands!

raccoon.about: {name} is a clever animal with a masked face and ringed tail. It has paws that work like hands to open lids and grab food. {name} lives near forests, rivers, and sometimes towns.
raccoon.funFact: Did you know? A {name} often washes food in water with its paws! Raccoons are active at night. They can remember puzzle solutions for years.
raccoon.try: Spell {name} and wash your hands like a raccoon!

skunk.about: {name} is black and white and lives in North America. If scared, it sprays a very strong smell to keep enemies away. {name} digs for insects and berries at night.
skunk.funFact: Did you know? A {name} warns enemies by stomping its feet first! Skunks can spray accurately several feet away. Their stripes warn predators to stay back.
skunk.try: Spell {name} and hold your nose playfully!

beaver.about: {name} is a brown animal that builds dams with sticks and mud. It has flat tail for swimming and orange teeth for gnawing wood. {name} lives in ponds and rivers.
beaver.funFact: Did you know? A {name}'s teeth are orange because of iron in the enamel! Beavers slap their tail on water to warn danger. Their dams create homes for fish and frogs.
beaver.try: Spell {name} and slap your leg like a flat tail splash!

bison.about: {name} is a huge shaggy wild cow that once roamed prairies in giant herds. It has a big head with horns and a hump on its shoulders. {name} eats grass on open plains.
bison.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can run fast despite looking so heavy! Bison are the largest land animals in North America. Their thick fur keeps them warm in snow.
bison.try: Spell {name} and lower your head like a strong bison!

boar.about: {name} is a wild pig with tough fur and sharp tusks. It digs the ground with its snout to find roots and nuts. {name} lives in forests and is most active at night.
boar.funFact: Did you know? A {name} has a strong snout for rooting in soil! Boars can run fast through the woods. Piglets of wild boars have stripes for camouflage.
boar.try: Spell {name} and pretend to dig with your hands!

badger.about: {name} is a sturdy animal with a striped face and short legs. It digs long tunnels underground called setts. {name} hunts at night for worms, mice, and insects.
badger.funFact: Did you know? A {name} is brave and will defend its burrow! Badgers keep their setts very clean. They can dig faster than a person with a shovel.
badger.try: Spell {name} and dig in the air with both hands!

crocodile.about: {name} lives in rivers and swamps with a long snout and powerful jaws. It floats quietly with eyes above water like bumps. {name} is a reptile with tough scaly skin.
crocodile.funFact: Did you know? A {name} has been around since dinosaur times! Crocodiles cannot chew — they tear food. Mother crocodiles carry babies in their mouth gently.
crocodile.try: Spell {name} and snap your arms gently like jaws!

orangutan.about: {name} is a red-orange ape with very long arms for swinging. It lives in rainforest trees in Borneo and Sumatra. {name} eats fruit and builds a new nest each night.
orangutan.funFact: Did you know? An {name} is among the smartest animals and uses tools! Orangutans share food with friends. They are mostly solitary unlike chimps.
orangutan.try: Spell {name} and swing your arms from side to side!

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is a bird — most birds have feathers and lay eggs!
detail.funFactTemplate: Many birds can fly, but penguins swim instead!
detail.tryTemplate: Flap your arms and spell {name} letter by letter!

eagle.about: {name} is a powerful bird of prey with sharp eyes and strong wings. It soars very high and can spot tiny animals far below. {name} builds a huge nest called an eyrie on cliffs or tall trees.
eagle.funFact: Did you know? An {name} can see much farther than you can! Its curved beak and strong talons help it catch food. Eagles stand for strength in many countries.
eagle.try: Spell {name} and soar with your arms spread wide!

duck.about: {name} is a water bird with webbed feet for swimming and a flat bill. It quacks and paddles on ponds and rivers. {name} often dips its head underwater to find plants and small creatures.
duck.funFact: Did you know? Duck feathers have special oil that keeps them dry! Baby ducks follow their mother in a line. Some ducks fly long distances when seasons change.
duck.try: Spell {name} and waddle while saying "quack quack"!

owl.about: {name} is a nighttime bird with big round eyes and soft feathers for silent flight. It hunts mice and insects when it is dark. {name} can turn its head far around to look without moving its body much.
owl.funFact: Did you know? An {name} turns its head because its eyes do not move much in their sockets! Owls hoot or screech to talk. Their hidden ears hear tiny sounds very well.

dove.about: {name} is a gentle bird with soft feathers and a peaceful cooing sound. It lives in pairs and pecks seeds on the ground. {name} is known as a symbol of peace and friendship.
dove.funFact: Did you know? Doves can fly fast and find their way home! They drink by sucking water without lifting their head high. Parent doves feed babies special crop milk.

swan.about: {name} is a graceful water bird with a long curved neck and often white feathers. It glides smoothly across lakes and ponds. {name} eats water plants and small creatures under the surface.
swan.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can sleep while floating on water! Swans often stay with the same partner for many years. They flap their wings loudly to warn of danger.
swan.try: Spell {name} and glide slowly with a long neck!

parrot.about: {name} is a bright colorful bird with a strong curved beak and feet that grip branches. It lives in warm places and loves nuts and fruit. {name} can copy sounds and sometimes human words.
parrot.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s live eighty years or more! Parrots use their feet like hands to hold food. Their bright colors help them hide among tropical leaves.
parrot.try: Spell {name} and squawk like a happy parrot!

flamingo.about: {name} is a tall pink bird with very long legs and a bent beak. It stands in shallow water and filters tiny shrimp and algae to eat. {name} often rests on one leg to save energy.
flamingo.funFact: Did you know? {name}s turn pink from the food they eat! They live in big groups called flamboyances. Flamingos build mud nests near water.
flamingo.try: Spell {name} and stand on one leg like a flamingo!

hen.about: {name} is a female farm bird that lays eggs we can cook and eat. She has feathers, a comb on her head, and scratches the ground for seeds and bugs. {name} clucks to her chicks and keeps them safe.
hen.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can lay an egg almost every day! Hens dust-bathe in dry dirt to stay clean. They remember faces and favorite spots.
hen.try: Spell {name} and cluck "cluck cluck" three times!

chick.about: {name} is a baby chicken with fluffy soft feathers and a tiny beak. It peeps when hungry or cold and follows the mother hen. {name} grows fast and soon gets bigger feathers.
chick.funFact: Did you know? Baby chicks can cheep before they hatch from the egg! Chicks snuggle under the hen for warmth. They learn to peck food in just a few days.

rooster.about: {name} is the male chicken with a tall red comb and colorful neck feathers. He crows loudly, often early in the morning, to call the flock. {name} watches for danger and struts proudly in the farmyard.
rooster.funFact: Did you know? A {name} crow can be heard far away! Roosters have sharp spurs on their legs for defense. They do not lay eggs — hens do.

penguin.about: {name} is a bird that cannot fly but swims fast in cold oceans. It has black-and-white feathers and flippers for paddling. {name} waddles on ice and huddles with friends to stay warm.
penguin.funFact: Did you know? {name}s leap out of water onto ice! They slide on their bellies — that is called tobogganing. Fathers often keep eggs warm on their feet.
penguin.try: Spell {name} and waddle with flippers at your sides!

peacock.about: {name} is a spectacular bird famous for its huge fan of colorful tail feathers with eye spots. The male spreads his tail to look big and beautiful. {name} lives in India and nearby places and calls with a loud cry.
peacock.funFact: Did you know? A {name} is India's national bird! The long tail is for display, not for long flying. Peacocks can fly short distances up to trees.
peacock.try: Spell {name} and fan out your arms like a shiny tail!

turkey.about: {name} is a large bird with a wobbly skin flap on its neck called a wattle. It gobbles and struts with its tail fanned out like a fan. {name} has strong legs and often lives on farms or in forests.
turkey.funFact: Did you know? A {name} gobble can be heard very far away! Turkeys have more feathers than most birds. Wild turkeys can run fast and fly short distances.

babyChick.about: {name} is a very young chicken with downy soft fluff and a tiny beak. It stays close to the mother and peeps for food and warmth. {name} needs a safe cozy place to grow.
babyChick.funFact: Did you know? {name}s can walk and eat soon after hatching! Their fluff is not waterproof like adult feathers. In a few weeks they grow real feathers.
babyChick.try: Spell {name} and cup your hands like holding a tiny chick!

bird.about: {name} is an animal with feathers, two wings, and a beak — most kinds can fly. It lays eggs in a nest and breathes with lungs like you do. {name} comes in many sizes from tiny hummingbirds to huge eagles.
bird.funFact: Did you know? Bird bones are hollow and light to help them fly! Birds sing to mark their home and call friends. Their feathers keep them warm and dry.
bird.try: Spell {name} and flap your arms like flying!

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} lives in the sea or ocean — look how it swims!
detail.funFactTemplate: The ocean is home to tiny fish and giant whales!
detail.tryTemplate: Make wave motions and spell {name} slowly!

fish.about: {name} is an animal that lives in water and breathes through gills on its sides. It has fins to swim and scales that often shine. {name} comes in many sizes, from tiny ones in bowls to huge ocean fish.
fish.funFact: Did you know? Some {name} can change color to hide! Fish swim by moving their tail side to side. A group of fish is called a school.
fish.try: Spell {name} and move your hand side to side like a swimming fish!

dolphin.about: {name} is a friendly sea animal known for being very smart. It swims in groups and jumps out of the water with a splash. {name} breathes air through a blowhole on top of its head.
dolphin.funFact: Did you know? {name}s talk with clicks and whistles! They sleep with one eye open. Dolphins help each other when a friend is hurt.
dolphin.try: Spell {name} and jump up with a happy splash!

whale.about: {name} is one of the biggest animals on Earth, even bigger than elephants. It lives in the ocean but must come up to breathe air. {name} sings long songs underwater that other whales can hear.
whale.funFact: Did you know? A blue {name} heart can be as big as a small car! Whales eat tiny creatures called krill or small fish. Baby whales drink rich milk from their mother.
whale.try: Spell {name} and blow air out like a spout from your nose!

shark.about: {name} is a strong ocean hunter with sharp teeth and a fin on its back. It has a special sense to feel movement in the water. {name} has been swimming in seas for millions of years.
shark.funFact: Did you know? {name} skin feels like sandpaper, not slimy! Sharks grow new teeth when old ones fall out. Most sharks are not dangerous to people.
shark.try: Spell {name} and put your hand on your head like a dorsal fin!

octopus.about: {name} is a soft sea animal with eight long arms covered in suckers. It can squeeze through very small holes and hides in rocks. {name} squirts dark ink to escape when scared.
octopus.funFact: Did you know? An {name} has three hearts and blue blood! It is very smart and can open jars. Octopuses change color and texture to camouflage.
octopus.try: Spell {name} and wiggle eight fingers like arms!

crab.about: {name} is a sea animal with a hard shell and two strong claws. It walks sideways on the beach or ocean floor. {name} hides under rocks and pinches if you bother it.
crab.funFact: Did you know? {name}s grow new shells as they get bigger! They breathe with gills. Crabs can run quickly sideways to escape.
crab.try: Spell {name} and scuttle sideways like a crab!

lobster.about: {name} is a large sea creature with a long body and big claws. It lives on the rocky ocean floor and hides in crevices. {name} has a hard shell and long antennae to feel around.
lobster.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s can live over 100 years! They walk on the sea bottom at night to hunt. Lobsters can regrow a lost claw over time.
lobster.try: Spell {name} and snap your hands like big claws!

pufferfish.about: {name} is a round fish that can puff up like a balloon when afraid. It has spines that stick out when inflated. {name} swims slowly in warm seas and coral reefs.
pufferfish.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s are poisonous if eaten! They fill with water or air to look too big to swallow. Pufferfish have beak-like teeth.
pufferfish.try: Spell {name} and puff your cheeks out big!

seal.about: {name} is a furry sea animal with flippers that swims and rests on beaches or ice. It has whiskers to feel fish in dark water. {name} barks or growls and loves to play in waves.
seal.funFact: Did you know? A {name} can hold its breath a long time underwater! Seal pups have fluffy white fur. Seals are great at catching fish.
seal.try: Spell {name} and clap your hands like flippers!

tropicalFish.about: {name} is a bright colorful fish that lives near warm coral reefs. It has beautiful patterns that help it hide among plants. {name} swims in sunny shallow water with many other fish.
tropicalFish.funFact: Did you know? Reef {name} often clean bigger fish by eating parasites! Their colors warn predators or attract mates. Many need clean warm oceans to survive.
tropicalFish.try: Spell {name} and swim with wiggly rainbow fingers!

seashell.about: {name} is the hard home that a soft sea animal once lived inside. Waves wash shells onto sandy beaches for you to find. {name} can be spiral, smooth, or bumpy in many colors.
seashell.funFact: Did you know? You can hear the ocean sound when you hold a {name} to your ear — that is really the air moving inside! Shells are made of calcium like chalk. Hermit crabs borrow empty shells.
seashell.try: Spell {name} and cup your ear like listening to the sea!

seaTurtle.about: {name} is a reptile with a hard shell that lives in the ocean. It has flippers to swim long distances and comes to sandy beaches to lay eggs. {name} can live many decades if kept safe.
seaTurtle.funFact: Did you know? A {name} returns to the beach where it was born to nest! They breathe air but can stay underwater a long time. Plastic bags in the ocean can hurt turtles.
seaTurtle.try: Spell {name} and paddle your arms like slow flippers!

shrimp.about: {name} is a small sea animal with a curved body and long antennae. It swims backward quickly by flipping its tail. {name} is food for fish, whales, and people in many places.
shrimp.funFact: Did you know? Some {name} can make a loud snapping sound with one claw! Shrimp come in many colors, even see-through. They clean parasites off fish on reefs.
shrimp.try: Spell {name} and flick your finger like a flipping tail!

squid.about: {name} is a fast sea animal with ten arms, including two longer tentacles. It shoots ink and jets through the water to escape hunters. {name} has big eyes and a soft body shaped like a torpedo.
squid.funFact: Did you know? Giant {name} can grow as long as a school bus! Squid change color with special cells in their skin. They are related to octopuses.
squid.try: Spell {name} and shoot backward with your arms behind you!

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is a fruit — sweet or tangy, full of vitamins!
detail.funFactTemplate: Fruits grow on trees, bushes, or vines!
detail.tryTemplate: Pretend to bite {name} and spell each letter!

apple.about: An {name} is a round crunchy fruit that grows on trees. It can be red, green, or yellow and is sweet or a little tart. {name} gives you fiber and vitamins that help your body stay strong.
apple.funFact: Did you know? There are thousands of kinds of {name}s around the world! Apple trees can live for many years. An apple a day is a famous saying about staying healthy.
apple.try: Spell {name} and pretend to take a big crunchy bite!

greenApple.about: A {name} is a crisp green apple with a brighter, tangier taste than many red apples. It grows on the same kind of tree and is great for snacking. {name} is juicy and full of vitamins.
greenApple.funFact: Did you know? {name}s have less sugar than very sweet red apples! Some people love them in salads. Green apples stay firm longer in the fridge.
greenApple.try: Spell {name} and crunch your teeth together loudly!

banana.about: A {name} is a long curved yellow fruit with a soft sweet inside. It grows in big bunches on tall plants in warm places. {name} is easy to peel and gives you energy to play.
banana.funFact: Did you know? {name}s are berries in science, even though they look different! Monkeys and people both enjoy them. They have potassium that helps your muscles.
banana.try: Spell {name} and peel an imaginary banana slowly!

grapes.about: {name} are tiny round fruits that grow in big bunches on vines. They can be green, red, or purple and taste very sweet. {name} can be eaten fresh, dried as raisins, or as juice.
grapes.funFact: Did you know? A bunch of {name} can have hundreds of grapes! People have grown grapes for thousands of years. Grapevines need sunshine to ripen.
grapes.try: Spell {name} and pop one imaginary grape into your mouth!

orange.about: An {name} is a round citrus fruit with a bright orange peel and juicy sections inside. It is famous for vitamin C that helps keep you healthy. {name} grows on trees in warm sunny places.
orange.funFact: Did you know? {name} trees can have flowers and fruit at the same time! The peel has a strong fresh smell. Orange juice is a popular breakfast drink.
orange.try: Spell {name} and pretend to squeeze fresh juice!

lemon.about: A {name} is a small yellow citrus fruit that tastes very sour. Its juice is used in lemonade and cooking. {name} has lots of vitamin C and a shiny fragrant skin.
lemon.funFact: Did you know? {name} juice can help stop apples from turning brown! Sailors once used lemons to fight sickness at sea. Lemon trees have pretty white flowers.
lemon.try: Spell {name} and make a sour face, then smile!

watermelon.about: A {name} is a huge fruit with a green striped outside and sweet red inside. It is full of water, so it is very refreshing on hot days. {name} has black seeds, and some kinds have almost no seeds.
watermelon.funFact: Did you know? {name} is mostly water — it helps you stay hydrated! The biggest ones can weigh as much as a big dog. People love it at summer picnics.
watermelon.try: Spell {name} and pat your belly like a big round melon!

strawberry.about: A {name} is a sweet red fruit with tiny seeds on the outside and a green cap on top. It grows close to the ground on small plants. {name} is soft, juicy, and perfect in desserts.
strawberry.funFact: Did you know? {name} is the only fruit with seeds on the outside! Each one has about 200 seeds. Strawberries are loved in shortcake and smoothies.
strawberry.try: Spell {name} and draw a tiny heart shape in the air!

cherry.about: A {name} is a small shiny red fruit with a hard pit in the middle. It grows on trees and tastes very sweet when ripe. {name} can be one alone or two joined together on a stem.
cherry.funFact: Did you know? Cherry trees bloom with beautiful pink or white flowers in spring! Birds love cherries too. Some cherries are dark red, almost purple.
cherry.try: Spell {name} and pop an imaginary cherry in your mouth!

peach.about: A {name} is a soft fuzzy fruit with sweet golden flesh and a big stone inside. It smells wonderful when ripe. {name} grows on trees and is juicy to bite into.
peach.funFact: Did you know? {name} trees need cold winters before they fruit well! The fuzzy skin protects the fruit a little. Peaches are related to plums and apricots.
peach.try: Spell {name} and rub your cheek like soft peach fuzz!

mango.about: A {name} is called the king of fruits in India and is golden, sweet, and very juicy. It has one large flat seed in the center. {name} grows on big trees in hot climates.
mango.funFact: Did you know? There are hundreds of types of {name} with different flavors! Green mangoes are used in tangy pickles. The smell of ripe {name} fills the whole room.
mango.try: Spell {name} and say “yum!” like tasting a ripe slice!

pineapple.about: A {name} has a spiky golden outside and sweet yellow rings inside. It grows from a leafy plant on the ground, not on a tree. {name} is tropical and very juicy when fresh.
pineapple.funFact: Did you know? {name} takes a long time to grow — up to two years! Each plant makes only one pineapple. Pineapple juice is used in many drinks.
pineapple.try: Spell {name} and wear an imaginary spiky crown!

coconut.about: A {name} is a big brown hard fruit with white tasty flesh and sweet water inside when young. It grows on tall palm trees near beaches. {name} gives us milk, oil, and food in many countries.
coconut.funFact: Did you know? {name} water is a natural drink inside young coconuts! The husk is very strong. Coconuts can float in the ocean and travel far.
coconut.try: Spell {name} and pretend to drink fresh coconut water!

kiwi.about: A {name} is a small brown fuzzy fruit with bright green inside and tiny black seeds. It tastes sweet and a little tangy. {name} is full of vitamin C and fiber.
kiwi.funFact: Did you know? {name} was first called Chinese gooseberry! You can eat the skin on some kinds if you wash them well. One kiwi has more vitamin C than an orange.
kiwi.try: Spell {name} and scoop with an imaginary spoon!

pear.about: A {name} is a sweet fruit shaped like a bell, narrower at the top. It can be green, yellow, or brownish when ripe. {name} is juicy and grows on trees.
pear.funFact: Did you know? {name}s ripen best after they are picked! Pears have been grown for thousands of years. Some pears are very soft, others stay crisp.
pear.try: Spell {name} and hold an imaginary pear shape with your hands!

melon.about: A {name} is a big round sweet fruit with lots of water inside, like cantaloupe or honeydew. The flesh can be orange or pale green. {name} is perfect for a hot day snack.
melon.funFact: Did you know? {name}s grow on vines along the ground! The rind protects the soft inside. A cool slice of melon feels like a treat.
melon.try: Spell {name} and hug your arms around a big round shape!

avocado.about: An {name} is a green fruit with creamy flesh and one big seed in the middle. It is not very sweet but is very healthy for your heart and brain. {name} is used in salads, sandwiches, and guacamole.
avocado.funFact: Did you know? {name} is technically a berry! It has healthy fats that help you grow. Avocado trees need warm weather to thrive.
avocado.try: Spell {name} and spread your hands like mashing soft avocado!

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is a vegetable — healthy food that helps you grow strong!
detail.funFactTemplate: Eating colorful vegetables keeps your body happy!
detail.tryTemplate: Crunch your hands like eating veggies while spelling {name}!

carrot.about: A {name} is a crunchy orange root that grows under the soil. It is sweet and full of vitamin A that helps your eyes stay healthy. {name} can be eaten raw, cooked, or in juice.
carrot.funFact: Did you know? {name}s can be purple, yellow, or white, not only orange! Rabbits love to munch them. Carrots left in the ground can grow flowers in the second year.
carrot.try: Spell {name} and crunch your hands together like biting a carrot!

potato.about: A {name} is a starchy vegetable that grows underground as a tuber. It can be boiled, baked, mashed, or made into fries. {name} gives you energy and is eaten all over the world.
potato.funFact: Did you know? {name} plants have green leaves above ground while the potato hides below! There are thousands of potato types. French fries are a favorite snack made from potatoes.
potato.try: Spell {name} and pat your hands like mashing potatoes!

onion.about: An {name} has many layers inside a papery skin and adds flavor to soups and curries. Cutting it can make your eyes water. {name} grows under the ground like a bulb.
onion.funFact: Did you know? {name}s can make you cry because of a gas when they are cut! They were used as food for thousands of years. Onions can be red, white, or yellow.
onion.try: Spell {name} and pretend to wipe one eye and sniff!

garlic.about: {name} is made of small strong-smelling cloves bundled in a papery head. It adds flavor to food and is used in many recipes. {name} is also known in stories to keep away vampires!
garlic.funFact: Did you know? {name} is related to onions and leeks! Each clove can be planted to grow a new plant. Garlic has been used as medicine in old times.
garlic.try: Spell {name} and hold your nose playfully, then grin!

broccoli.about: {name} looks like tiny green trees on a thick stem and is one of the healthiest vegetables. It is full of vitamins and fiber. {name} can be steamed, roasted, or eaten with dip.
broccoli.funFact: Did you know? {name} is a flower vegetable — we eat the buds before they bloom! It is in the same family as cabbage. One cup has lots of vitamin C.
broccoli.try: Spell {name} and stand tall like a little green tree!

lettuce.about: {name} has soft green leaves used in salads and sandwiches. It grows quickly and likes cool weather. {name} is crunchy and full of water.
lettuce.funFact: Did you know? There are many types of {name}, like romaine and iceberg! Lettuce was eaten by ancient kings. It grows from tiny seeds in rows.
lettuce.try: Spell {name} and rustle your hands like salad leaves!

cucumber.about: A {name} is a long cool green vegetable with lots of water inside. It is crunchy and mild, great in salads and raita. {name} grows on a vine in gardens.
cucumber.funFact: Did you know? {name} slices can cool tired eyes in stories and spa tricks! Pickles are often made from cucumbers. They grow very fast in summer.
cucumber.try: Spell {name} and make a cool “ahhh” face like a refreshing bite!

corn.about: {name} has sweet yellow kernels on a cob and grows on tall stalks in fields. It can be boiled, grilled, or popped into popcorn. {name} is a grain that people eat as a vegetable.
corn.funFact: Did you know? Each {name} kernel is a seed! Popcorn pops when the water inside heats up. Corn plants can grow taller than you.
corn.try: Spell {name} and pretend to twist an imaginary corn cob!

pumpkin.about: A {name} is a big orange vegetable with thick flesh and many seeds inside. It is used in pies, soups, and Halloween lanterns. {name} grows on a vine along the ground.
pumpkin.funFact: Did you know? Giant {name}s can weigh hundreds of kilograms in contests! Pumpkin seeds are tasty when roasted. Native people used pumpkins for food long ago.
pumpkin.try: Spell {name} and carve a happy face in the air!

eggplant.about: An {name} is a shiny purple vegetable with soft flesh used in curries and grilled dishes. It grows on a bush-like plant with pretty leaves. {name} soaks up flavors when it cooks.
eggplant.funFact: Did you know? {name} can also be white or striped, not only purple! It is called brinjal in India. Eggplants love warm sunny weather.
eggplant.try: Spell {name} and rub your hands on a smooth purple surface!

mushroom.about: A {name} is not a plant but a fungus that grows in damp places and forests. It comes in many shapes and colors, like button, portobello, and shiitake. {name} adds a savory taste to pizza and soups.
mushroom.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s glow in the dark! Never eat wild mushrooms without an expert — some are poisonous. Mushrooms grow very fast overnight.
mushroom.try: Spell {name} and pop up from a squat like a mushroom!

chili.about: A {name} is a small hot pepper that can be red or green and makes food spicy. The heat comes from capsaicin inside. {name} is used carefully in curries and sauces.
chili.funFact: Did you know? Birds can eat hot {name}s without feeling the burn! Milk helps cool your mouth if it is too spicy. Chili plants love warm weather.
chili.try: Spell {name} and fan your tongue after one tiny pretend bite!

tomato.about: A {name} is a red juicy fruit that we often use like a vegetable in salads, ketchup, and sauce. It grows on a vine and ripens in the sun. {name} is full of vitamins and lycopene.
tomato.funFact: Did you know? Botanically a {name} is a fruit, not a vegetable! Tomato plants can grow very tall with support. Ketchup is made from millions of tomatoes.
tomato.try: Spell {name} and roll your hands like a round tomato!

peanut.about: A {name} is not a nut but a legume that grows underground in shells. It is crunchy and full of protein and healthy fats. {name} is used to make peanut butter and snacks.
peanut.funFact: Did you know? {name} plants flower above ground but the peanuts form below! George Washington Carver found many uses for peanuts. Peanut butter sandwiches are popular worldwide.
peanut.try: Spell {name} and spread your palms like peanut butter on bread!

sweetPotato.about: A {name} has orange sweet flesh and grows underground like a potato but tastes sweeter. It is baked, mashed, or made into fries. {name} has vitamins that help your body grow.
sweetPotato.funFact: Did you know? {name} leaves are also edible in some places! They are popular in many countries at holiday meals. Orange color comes from beta-carotene like carrots.
sweetPotato.try: Spell {name} and hug a warm imaginary baked sweet potato!

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is a flower — pretty petals and often a nice smell!
detail.funFactTemplate: Bees visit flowers to help plants grow!
detail.tryTemplate: Smell an imaginary flower and spell {name}!

rose.about: {name} is a famous flower with soft petals, often red or pink, and a sweet smell. It grows on a bush with thorns on the stem to protect it. {name} is a gift flower for love and friendship.
rose.funFact: Did you know? {name} petals can be used to make perfume! There are thousands of types of roses. Bees and butterflies visit roses for nectar.
rose.try: Spell {name} and sniff an imaginary sweet flower!

tulip.about: {name} is a spring flower shaped like a cup on a tall straight stem. It comes in red, yellow, pink, purple, and more. {name} grows from a bulb underground and opens in the sunshine.
tulip.funFact: Did you know? {name}s are loved in the Netherlands where huge fields bloom! Each bulb can grow one flower per year. Tulips close at night like they are sleeping.
tulip.try: Spell {name} and stand tall with cupped hands!

daisy.about: {name} is a cheerful flower with white petals around a yellow center. It grows in grass and meadows and is easy to spot. {name} looks like a little sun on the ground.
daisy.funFact: Did you know? You can make a daisy chain by linking stems together! Daisies close at night and open in the morning. Their name means "day's eye."
daisy.try: Spell {name} and twirl like a sunny flower!

sunflower.about: {name} is a tall flower with a big yellow face that follows the sun across the sky. Its seeds are tasty for birds and people. {name} can grow taller than you in one summer.
sunflower.funFact: Did you know? One {name} head can have hundreds of seeds! Young sunflowers turn to face the sun each day. Sunflower oil is used in cooking.
sunflower.try: Spell {name} and stretch tall toward the sky!

blossom.about: {name} means flowers opening on trees in spring, like cherry or apple trees. Pink and white petals fall like soft snow in the wind. {name} tells us warm days are coming after winter.
blossom.funFact: Did you know? Cherry {name} festivals are celebrated in Japan! Blossoms last only a short time, so people enjoy them quickly. Bees love fresh blossoms for nectar.
blossom.try: Spell {name} and let your fingers drift down like petals!

hibiscus.about: {name} is a big tropical flower with wide petals, often red, pink, or yellow. It grows in warm places and can be made into a tangy drink. {name} lasts only a day or two on the plant.
hibiscus.funFact: Did you know? In some places people wear a {name} behind the ear! Hummingbirds love hibiscus nectar. The flower has a long tube for sipping.
hibiscus.try: Spell {name} and spread your hands wide like big petals!

bouquet.about: {name} is a bunch of flowers tied together as a pretty gift. People give it on birthdays, weddings, or to say thank you. {name} smells wonderful and brightens any room.
bouquet.funFact: Did you know? Florists choose flowers that look good together in a {name}! Some flowers last longer in water than others. A ribbon makes a bouquet extra special.
bouquet.try: Spell {name} and pretend to give flowers to a friend!

dryFlower.about: {name} is a flower that has lost its water and turned brown or crispy, but it can still look beautiful. People press or hang flowers to dry them for crafts. {name} reminds us flowers do not last forever, but memories can.
dryFlower.funFact: Did you know? Dried {name}s can stay pretty for years in a vase! Pressing flowers in a heavy book flattens them. Dry petals are used in potpourri for smell.
dryFlower.try: Spell {name} and gently crumble imaginary petals in your fingers!

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is part of nature — earth, sky, plants, and places!
detail.funFactTemplate: Nature is all around us — even in your own backyard!
detail.tryTemplate: Point outside and spell {name} — one letter at a time!

earth.about: {name} is our home planet, the round world we live on. It has land, oceans, air, and life everywhere. {name} spins in space around the sun and gives us day and night.
earth.funFact: Did you know? {name} is mostly covered by water — about seven tenths! It is the only planet we know with so much life. We must keep {name} clean and healthy.
earth.try: Spell {name} and spin slowly in a circle like our planet!

tree.about: {name} is a tall plant with a woody trunk, branches, and leaves. It makes oxygen we breathe and gives shade on hot days. {name} is home to birds, insects, and squirrels.
tree.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s live for thousands of years! Roots drink water deep underground. Trees grow rings inside the trunk — one per year.
tree.try: Spell {name} and stand still with arms like branches!

mountain.about: {name} is a very high part of land that rises toward the sky. It can be rocky, snowy, or covered with forests. {name} takes a long time to climb and has cool air at the top.
mountain.funFact: Did you know? The tallest {name} on Earth is Mount Everest! Mountains form when Earth's plates push together. Goats and eagles live on steep mountains.
mountain.try: Spell {name} and point your hands up like a peak!

snowMountain.about: {name} is a mountain top covered with white snow and ice all year or in winter. It shines in the sun and feeds rivers when snow melts. {name} is cold and beautiful but hard to climb.
snowMountain.funFact: Did you know? Snow on a {name} reflects bright light — wear sunglasses! Avalanches are fast slides of snow. Skiing happens on snowy mountains.
snowMountain.try: Spell {name} and shiver gently like you feel the cold!

volcano.about: {name} is a mountain that can erupt hot melted rock called lava from inside Earth. It also sends ash and gases high into the sky. {name} builds new land when lava cools into rock.
volcano.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}es sleep for hundreds of years then wake up! Lava glows red and orange at night. Volcanic soil helps plants grow well.
volcano.try: Spell {name} and raise your arms like a puff of ash!

desert.about: {name} is a dry place with little rain, often hot sand or rocky ground. Cactus and camels are built to live with very little water. {name} can be cold at night even if it is hot in the day.
desert.funFact: Did you know? The Sahara is the world's largest hot {name}! Some deserts have sand dunes shaped by wind. Desert animals hide in the day and move at night.
desert.try: Spell {name} and shade your eyes like bright sun!

island.about: {name} is land with water all around it — in a sea, lake, or river. It can be tiny with one tree or huge like a country. {name} may have beaches, forests, and animals found nowhere else.
island.funFact: Did you know? Hawaii is a chain of volcanic {name}s! Some islands are made of coral. People reach islands by boat or plane.
island.try: Spell {name} and draw a circle of water with your finger!

beach.about: {name} is where land meets the sea with soft sand or pebbles. Waves roll in and out and leave shells behind. {name} is fun for building sandcastles, swimming, and watching sunsets.
beach.funFact: Did you know? Waves at the {name} are caused by wind far away! Tides make the water level rise and fall. Crabs and seagulls live on beaches.
beach.try: Spell {name} and make wave motions with your hands!

valley.about: {name} is low land between hills or mountains, often with a river running through. It can be green with farms and flowers. {name} is sheltered from strong wind and good for growing food.
valley.funFact: Did you know? Rivers carve {name}s over thousands of years! Some valleys are deep canyons with steep walls. Animals graze in peaceful valleys.
valley.try: Spell {name} and make your hands into hills with a dip between!

rock.about: {name} is hard natural stone found on mountains, beaches, and underground. It can be smooth, rough, shiny, or full of crystals. {name} has been part of Earth for millions of years.
rock.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s are used to build houses and roads! Fossils of ancient plants and animals can hide inside rock. Gold and gems form in special rocks.
rock.try: Spell {name} and tap your fist like something very hard!

wood.about: {name} comes from tree trunks and is used to build homes, furniture, and toys. It can be carved, sanded, and painted. {name} smells nice when fresh and floats on water.
wood.funFact: Did you know? {name} is strong but can rot if wet too long! Paper also comes from wood pulp. Beavers chew wood to build dams.
wood.try: Spell {name} and knock on an imaginary wooden table!

wheatField.about: {name} is a large farm area where golden wheat plants grow in rows. Wind makes the stalks sway like waves. {name} becomes flour for bread, roti, and pasta after harvest.
wheatField.funFact: Did you know? Wheat is one of the oldest crops people grew! A {name} can feed many families. Combine machines cut wheat quickly at harvest time.
wheatField.try: Spell {name} and sway side to side like golden stalks!

herb.about: {name} is a small plant with leaves that smell strong and taste good in food. Mint, basil, and coriander are herbs. {name} can grow in gardens, pots, or wild meadows.
herb.funFact: Did you know? Herbs have been used as medicine for thousands of years! Rubbing a leaf releases the smell. Bees like herb flowers too.
herb.try: Spell {name} and rub your fingers together like smelling leaves!

leaf.about: {name} is the flat green part of a plant that catches sunlight to make food. It has veins like little roads inside. {name} falls in autumn and grows again in spring on many trees.
leaf.funFact: Did you know? No two {name}s are exactly alike on some trees! Leaves make oxygen for us. Green color comes from chlorophyll.
leaf.try: Spell {name} and flutter your hand down like a falling leaf!

seedling.about: {name} is a baby plant just sprouting from a seed in the soil. It has tiny roots below and small leaves reaching for light. {name} needs water, sun, and care to grow big.
seedling.funFact: Did you know? A bean {name} can grow a few centimeters in one day! Seeds hold food inside until roots form. Never step on young seedlings in a garden.
seedling.try: Spell {name} and crouch small, then slowly stand up growing!

plant.about: {name} is a living thing that grows in soil and makes its own food from sunlight. It has roots, stems, and leaves or flowers. {name} gives us oxygen, food, and shade.
plant.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}s eat insects, like the Venus flytrap! Plants cannot walk but they bend toward light. Water travels up the stem like a straw.
plant.try: Spell {name} and reach toward the sun with both hands!

camping.about: {name} means sleeping outdoors in a tent or under the stars with family or friends. You cook on a fire, tell stories, and listen to night sounds. {name} helps you enjoy forests, lakes, and fresh air.
camping.funFact: Did you know? Always pack water and a flashlight for {name}! Leave no trash in nature. You might hear owls or see fireflies at night.
camping.try: Spell {name} and pretend to zip up a cozy tent!

bridge.about: {name} is a structure that crosses over a river, road, or valley so people can walk or drive across. It can be made of stone, steel, or wood. {name} connects two places that water or depth separated.
bridge.funFact: Did you know? Some {name}es are hundreds of years old! Suspension bridges hang from strong cables. Beavers build small bridge-like dams too.
bridge.try: Spell {name} and walk your fingers across an imaginary bridge!

hut.about: {name} is a small simple house, often made of wood, mud, or grass. People use it in villages, farms, or near beaches. {name} has a roof to stay dry and walls to block wind.
hut.funFact: Did you know? {name}s stay cool in hot places with thick walls! Some huts are on stilts above water. Families have lived in huts for thousands of years.
hut.try: Spell {name} and shape a roof with your hands over your head!

tent.about: {name} is a portable shelter made of fabric stretched over poles. Campers set it up quickly for sleeping outdoors. {name} keeps rain out and bugs away while you hear nature outside.
tent.funFact: Did you know? A {name} should be pegged down so wind does not blow it away! Inside is cozy with a sleeping bag. Take shoes off before going in to keep mud out.
tent.try: Spell {name} and pull two corners like setting up fabric!

mountFuji.about: {name} is Japan's famous tall volcano with a snowy cone shape. It is a sacred mountain that artists have painted for centuries. {name} can be seen from Tokyo on clear days.
mountFuji.funFact: Did you know? Thousands climb {name} each summer! It last erupted long ago but is still a volcano. The mountain is a symbol of Japan.
mountFuji.try: Spell {name} and make a triangle peak with your hands!

sun.about: The {name} is a giant star that gives Earth light and warmth. It rises in the morning and sets in the evening, making day and night. {name} helps plants grow and keeps us from freezing.
sun.funFact: Did you know? Never stare at the {name} — it can hurt your eyes! The sun is 150 million kilometers away. Without the sun, Earth would be dark and cold.
sun.try: Spell {name} and draw a big bright circle in the air!

moon.about: The {name} is Earth's companion in the sky that reflects sunlight so we see it glow at night. It changes shape from thin crescent to full round and back. {name} pulls on oceans to make tides.
moon.funFact: Did you know? Astronauts walked on the {name} in 1969! The same side of the moon always faces Earth. A full moon is bright enough to cast shadows.
moon.try: Spell {name} and cup your hands like a round glowing moon!

star.about: A {name} is a huge ball of hot gas far away in space that twinkles in our night sky. The sun is the closest star to us. {name}s make patterns called constellations that people name like the Big Dipper.
star.funFact: Did you know? Light from a {name} can travel for years before we see it! Stars are born in clouds of gas and dust. Wishing on a star is a fun tradition.
star.try: Spell {name} and twinkle your fingers in the dark!

saturn.about: {name} is a huge planet far from Earth with beautiful rings made of ice and rock. It is a gas giant like Jupiter and spins very fast. {name} has many moons orbiting around it.
saturn.funFact: Did you know? {name}'s rings are only meters thick but very wide! You cannot stand on Saturn — there is no solid ground. Telescopes show its rings clearly.
saturn.try: Spell {name} and draw rings around an imaginary ball!

sparkle.about: {name} is a quick flash of light, like stars twinkling or sun on water. Fireworks and glitter sparkle at celebrations. {name} catches your eye and feels magical for a moment.
sparkle.funFact: Did you know? Snow can {name} in sunlight like diamonds! Fish scales sparkle in the sea. A smile can sparkle in someone's eyes.
sparkle.try: Spell {name} and blink your fingers like tiny flashes!

nightSky.about: The {name} is the dark dome above us after sunset filled with stars, the moon, and sometimes planets. On clear nights you see the Milky Way as a cloudy band. {name} changes with seasons and weather.
nightSky.funFact: Did you know? Light pollution from cities hides many stars in the {name}! Ancient people used stars to navigate. Meteors are shooting stars burning in the air.
nightSky.try: Spell {name} and look up while spelling each letter slowly!

weather.title: Weather & seasons

detail.aboutTemplate: Learning about {name} helps you understand the sky, the air around you, and how the year changes. Weather and seasons are part of nature — when you know the words, they feel less confusing and more fun to watch.
detail.funFactTemplate: Did you know? Weather can change in one day — sunshine in the morning and rain in the afternoon! Grown-ups check the weather to choose clothes, plan trips, and keep you safe and comfortable.
detail.tryTemplate: With a grown-up, look out a window or picture the sky. Say "{name}" slowly three times. Tell someone one thing you see, hear, or feel that fits {name} today.

sunny.about: Sunny weather means the sun is shining and the sky looks bright. You may feel warm on your skin, see sharp shadows, and want to play outside. Sunny days help plants grow because they use sunlight to make food.
sunny.funFact: Did you know? The sun is a star very far away — its light still reaches Earth! On very sunny days, drinking water, wearing a hat, and sitting in shade help your body stay cool.
sunny.try: Hold your hand above your eyes like a little visor. Say "{name}!" and name one sunny thing you like — bright sky, warm light, or long shadows.

rainy.about: Rainy weather means water falls from clouds as raindrops. The sky may look gray, the ground gets wet, and you might hear pitter-patter on roofs and windows. Rain fills rivers and helps plants and animals get the water they need.
rainy.funFact: Did you know? Rain starts when tiny drops inside clouds join together until they are heavy enough to fall! Some rainy days are soft and gentle; others bring lots of rain for hours.
rainy.try: Tap your fingers on a table: pitter-patter, pitter-patter. Say "{name}!" and draw a cloud with rain lines in the air using your finger.

cloudy.about: Cloudy weather means many clouds cover the sky, so the sun may hide or look dim. The air can feel cool and calm. Clouds are not cotton — they are made of tiny water drops floating high up.
cloudy.funFact: Did you know? Clouds can look like animals, ships, or dragons if you use your imagination! Gray clouds often mean rain might come later, but not always.
cloudy.try: Lie on your back or look up. Say "{name}!" and tell someone what shape you see in the clouds — or draw your favorite cloud shape.

windy.about: Windy weather means air moves fast around you. Trees may sway, leaves may fly, and kites can pull on their string. Wind can feel exciting on your face — hold your hat so it does not blow away!
windy.funFact: Did you know? Wind can spin big windmills to help make electricity in some places! Birds often glide on windy days to save energy.
windy.try: Blow out slowly like birthday candles — feel the air move. Say "{name}!" and wave your arms like a flag in the wind.

storm.about: A storm is strong weather with heavy wind, rain, and sometimes thunder and lightning. Storms can sound loud, but you are safest inside a strong building with a grown-up. Storms usually pass after a while.
storm.funFact: Did you know? Lightning is a huge spark of electricity in the sky! Thunder is the sound that comes after — light travels faster than sound, so we see flash before we hear boom.
storm.try: Stay indoors with a grown-up. When you hear thunder, count slowly: "1 elephant, 2 elephant…" More seconds means the storm is farther away.

snow.about: Snow is frozen water that falls in soft white flakes when the air is very cold. It can cover the ground like a blanket and crunch under boots. In snowy places, kids build snowmen and slide on sleds.
snow.funFact: Did you know? Every snowflake has its own pattern — no two are exactly alike! Snow reflects light, so sunny snowy days can feel extra bright.
snow.try: Pretend snowflakes fall on your tongue — catch one gently in your imagination. Say "{name}!" and swirl your fingers down like falling flakes.

fog.about: Fog is a thick mist close to the ground that makes far things hard to see. It can feel quiet and mysterious, like walking inside a soft gray cloud. Fog often happens in the early morning or near water.
fog.funFact: Did you know? Fog is made of tiny water drops, just like clouds — but low down! Drivers slow down and use special lights because they cannot see far.
fog.try: Wave your hand slowly in front of your face. Say "{name}!" and pretend the world disappears behind your hand like mist.

hotDay.about: A hot day means the air feels very warm on your skin. You might sweat, feel thirsty, and want cool water or shade. Hot days happen often in summer or in sunny places at noon.
hotDay.funFact: Did you know? Your body cools itself by sweating — the water on your skin helps heat go away! Light clothes and drinking water help on hot days.
hotDay.try: Fan your face with your hand and sip water if a grown-up says yes. Say "{name}!" and name one cool place you like — shade, fan, or cold drink.

coldDay.about: A cold day means the air feels chilly on your cheeks and fingers. You might shiver and want a sweater, socks, or a warm blanket. Cold days are common in winter or early morning.
coldDay.funFact: Did you know? Some animals grow thicker fur or feathers before cold weather! Your body keeps warm by shivering a little — moving and hugging help too.
coldDay.try: Hug yourself gently and say "Brrr, cold day!" Rub your hands together slowly to feel warmth. Tell a grown-up if you need another layer.

rainbow.about: A rainbow is a colorful arc in the sky when sunlight shines through raindrops. You may see red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and more — like a bridge made of light. Rainbows often appear when sun and rain happen together.
rainbow.funFact: Did you know? A full rainbow is actually a circle — we usually see only the top part! You cannot walk to the end of a rainbow; it moves as you move.
rainbow.try: Say the rainbow colors out loud in order. Draw a big arc in the air with your finger and say "{name}!"

thunder.about: Thunder is the deep rumbling sound that comes after lightning in the sky. It can sound loud or scary, but if you are inside with a grown-up, you are usually safe. Thunder tells us a storm is nearby or passing by.
thunder.funFact: Did you know? A big boom can mean lightning was close, and a quiet rumble can mean it was farther away! Counting seconds after a flash helps grown-ups guess the distance.
thunder.try: If a storm is far away, cover your ears softly and whisper "boom" like gentle thunder. Say "{name}!" and stay calm indoors with someone you trust.

drizzle.about: Drizzle is very light, gentle rain with tiny drops. The ground may get damp without big puddles. Drizzle can last a long time and feels soft on your skin if you wear a hood.
drizzle.funFact: Did you know? Drizzle drops are smaller than normal raindrops — they fall slowly! Plants still love drizzle because it waters them bit by bit.
drizzle.try: Make tiny tapping sounds on your arm with one finger — drip, drip, drip. Say "{name}!" and imagine mist on your cheeks.

hail.about: Hail is ice that falls in small round pieces during strong storms. Hailstones can be tiny like peas or bigger — they bounce and make loud taps on roofs. Stay indoors when hail falls; it can hurt.
hail.funFact: Did you know? Hail forms when raindrops are tossed up and down inside cold clouds until they freeze in layers! That is why hail looks like little ice balls.
hail.try: Pretend tiny ice balls bounce in your cupped hands — pat-pat-pat. Say "{name}!" and remember: when ice falls from the sky, stay inside with a grown-up.

breeze.about: A gentle breeze is a soft, light wind that tickles your skin without pushing hard. It can feel cool on a warm day and make leaves rustle quietly. Breezes are friendly wind — not scary storms.
breeze.funFact: Did you know? Sailboats and kites use breezes to move! A breeze can carry the smell of flowers or fresh grass to your nose.
breeze.try: Close your eyes and breathe in slowly through your nose. Feel air on your cheeks and say "{name}!" Move your fingers like leaves waving.

humid.about: Humid weather means the air holds lots of water, so it can feel sticky on your skin. Your hair might curl, and sweat may not dry quickly. Humid days often come before rain in many places.
humid.funFact: Did you know? Tropical places near the ocean often feel humid much of the year! Even when you do not see rain, humid air can make you feel damp.
humid.try: Gently wipe your forehead and say "Humid — so sticky today!" Drink water and tell a grown-up how the air feels on your skin.

clearSky.about: A clear sky has few or no clouds, so you can see the sun, moon, or stars clearly. Clear days feel open and bright; clear nights are perfect for spotting the moon and stars with a grown-up.
clearSky.funFact: Did you know? Pilots and farmers like clear skies because they can see far! Pollution or smoke can hide stars — dark country skies show the most stars.
clearSky.try: Look up (safely, never stare at the bright sun). Trace one star or the moon shape with your finger and say "{name}!"

monsoon.about: Monsoon is a special rainy season in India and nearby places. Heavy rains water farms, fill rivers, and cool the hot air. Roads can splash, so kids often play indoors with stories and games.
monsoon.funFact: Did you know? Monsoon rains help rice and many crops grow — farmers depend on them! Frogs and peacocks are often louder during monsoon.
monsoon.try: Listen to real rain or pretend rain sounds with your fingers. Say "{name}!" and draw one thing that needs rain — a plant, river, or farm.

spring.about: Spring is a season after winter when weather warms up and new life appears. Flowers bloom, trees grow fresh leaves, and baby animals may be born. Spring days can be sunny, rainy, or breezy — nature wakes up.
spring.funFact: Did you know? In spring, days slowly get longer — more daylight for play after school! Many festivals celebrate spring and new beginnings.
spring.try: Pretend to plant a seed in the ground, water it, and grow tall like a flower. Say "{name}!" and name one new thing you see outside in spring.

summer.about: Summer is the warmest season in many places. Kids may swim, eat cold treats, wear light clothes, and have holidays from school. Summer sun is strong, so shade and water matter.
summer.funFact: Did you know? In summer, the sun stays up longer in the evening in many countries! Mangoes and ice pops are favorite summer treats in lots of homes.
summer.try: Pretend to hold a cold juicy fruit and say "Yum, summer!" Fan yourself and tell one fun summer plan — pool, park, or picnic.

autumn.about: Autumn (also called fall) is a season when air turns cooler and some leaves change color — gold, orange, and red — then drift to the ground. Days get shorter and harvest time comes on farms.
autumn.funFact: Did you know? Some birds fly long distances in autumn to find warmer places! Squirrels collect nuts to eat when food is harder to find.
autumn.try: Let your arms float down slowly like falling leaves. Say "{name}!" and crunch imaginary leaves under your feet — crunch, crunch!

winter.about: Winter is the coldest season in many places. You may wear sweaters, drink warm soup, and see frost on grass in the morning. Some regions get snow; others get chilly wind and fog.
winter.funFact: Did you know? In winter, nights are longer — cozy story time! Animals like bears may sleep more in winter to save energy where it is very cold.
winter.try: Rub your hands together fast and feel warmth. Say "{name}!" and name one cozy winter thing — blanket, soup, or warm socks.

days.title: Days of the Week

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is one of the seven days that make a full week. Learning day names helps children understand school routines, play time, and family plans.
detail.funFactTemplate: Did you know? Days always move in the same order, then repeat again every week. Knowing {name} helps you talk about yesterday, today, and tomorrow.
detail.tryTemplate: Say "{name}" slowly three times. Tell a grown-up one thing you usually do on {name}.

monday.about: Monday usually starts a new school week for many children. After the weekend, Monday feels like a fresh beginning for learning and new goals.
monday.funFact: Did you know? The name Monday comes from the Moon in old languages. Many people make Monday to-do lists for the week.
monday.try: Stretch both arms up like a fresh start and say "{name}!"

tuesday.about: Tuesday is the second day of the school week in many places. It is a good day to keep learning habits strong and continue class work.
tuesday.funFact: Did you know? In many languages, Tuesday is linked to strength or courage. Small steady effort on Tuesday helps the whole week go smoothly.
tuesday.try: Clap 2 times and say "{name}!" Then name one class you enjoy.

wednesday.about: Wednesday sits in the middle of the week. By Wednesday, children have already done part of their work and can feel proud of their progress.
wednesday.funFact: Did you know? Wednesday is often called mid-week. Many people check plans on Wednesday to stay organized for the rest of the week.
wednesday.try: Take one small hop and say "{name}!" Then show 3 fingers for mid-week energy.

thursday.about: Thursday comes after Wednesday and before Friday. It is often a focused day for completing homework, projects, and class practice.
thursday.funFact: Did you know? In some schools, Thursday has special activity periods like sports, art, or music.
thursday.try: Give yourself a thumbs-up and say "{name}!"

friday.about: Friday is often the last school day before the weekend. Many children feel excited because rest and family time are near.
friday.funFact: Did you know? Friday evenings are popular for family meals and fun plans in many homes.
friday.try: Do a tiny happy dance and say "{name}!"

saturday.about: Saturday is a weekend day in many places. It can be used for play, hobbies, family visits, markets, or extra rest.
saturday.funFact: Did you know? Parks, playgrounds, and sports classes are often busiest on Saturdays.
saturday.try: Say "{name}!" and name one fun activity you want to do this weekend.

sunday.about: Sunday is often a quiet family day before a new week starts. Many people rest, pray, travel, or prepare school things for Monday.
sunday.funFact: Did you know? In many calendars, Sunday is marked as a special rest day.
sunday.try: Take a deep breath, smile softly, and say "{name}!"

months.readTogether: Point to the word and read it together!
months.title: Months of the Year

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is one of the twelve months in a year. Learning month names helps children understand birthdays, seasons, school events, and festivals.
detail.funFactTemplate: Did you know? Months repeat in the same order every year. Knowing {name} helps you talk about when events happened or will happen.
detail.tryTemplate: Say "{name}" slowly. Clap once for each syllable and tell a grown-up one event in {name}.

january.about: January is the first month of the year. It often feels like a new beginning with new calendars, school terms, and goals.
january.funFact: Did you know? New Year celebrations happen at the start of January in many countries.
january.try: Say "{name}!" and pretend to flip to a new calendar page.

february.about: February is the second month and the shortest month of the year. It usually has 28 days, and sometimes 29 in a leap year.
february.funFact: Did you know? Leap year comes every four years and gives February one extra day.
february.try: Count to 2 on your fingers and say "{name}!"

march.about: March is the third month. In many places, weather starts changing and spring signs appear, while in India many festivals may happen around this time.
march.funFact: Did you know? In many regions, school exams or final terms begin around March.
march.try: Say "{name}!" and pretend flowers are starting to bloom.

april.about: April is the fourth month. Many places feel warmer in April, and trees and gardens become greener.
april.funFact: Did you know? April is often linked with changing weather, from sunny mornings to sudden rain.
april.try: Draw a tiny flower in the air and say "{name}!"

may.about: May is the fifth month and is often hot in many parts of India. Many children enjoy summer holidays during this month.
may.funFact: Did you know? Mango season is strong in May in many places, making it a favorite month for fruit lovers.
may.try: Say "{name}!" and pretend to fan yourself in warm weather.

june.about: June is the sixth month. In many schools, new sessions or classes begin around June, and rains may start in some regions.
june.funFact: Did you know? June has long daylight in many countries, giving more bright time in the evening.
june.try: Say "{name}!" and mimic carrying a school bag proudly.

july.about: July is the seventh month. In many places, monsoon rain becomes stronger and children carry umbrellas and raincoats.
july.funFact: Did you know? Farmers welcome July rains because crops need steady water.
july.try: Tap your fingers like rain and say "{name}!"

august.about: August is the eighth month. It is a festive month in India with patriotic celebrations and school cultural activities.
august.funFact: Did you know? India celebrates Independence Day in August.
august.try: Wave an imaginary flag and say "{name}!"

september.about: September is the ninth month. Schools are usually active with studies, assignments, and regular routines.
september.funFact: Did you know? In many places, weather starts shifting slowly after peak monsoon.
september.try: Say "{name}!" and open an imaginary notebook to study.

october.about: October is the tenth month and often brings pleasant weather in many regions. It is also a festive period in India for many families.
october.funFact: Did you know? Several major Indian festivals often fall in October, making it colorful and joyful.
october.try: Smile wide, say "{name}!" and pretend to light a festival lamp safely with a grown-up.

november.about: November is the eleventh month. The air can feel cooler in many places, and schools continue with projects and events.
november.funFact: Did you know? November often has clear skies in many regions after rainy months.
november.try: Wrap your arms like a light sweater hug and say "{name}!"

december.about: December is the twelfth and last month of the year. Many families celebrate holidays, review memories, and prepare for a new year.
december.funFact: Did you know? Year-end celebrations happen in December across many cultures and communities.
december.try: Count down 3, 2, 1 and say "{name}!" with a cheerful clap.

family.readTogether: Point to the word and read it together!
family.title: Family Members

detail.aboutTemplate: {name} is an important family member. Family members care for each other, share responsibilities, and help children feel safe, loved, and confident.
detail.funFactTemplate: Did you know? Every family is special. Even if families look different, love, respect, and helping each other make a family strong.
detail.tryTemplate: Say "{name}" slowly three times. Point to a family photo or tell a grown-up one kind thing this person does.
